items.title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
items.summary: Root cause analysis (RCA) of microservice failures has attracted many LLM agents whose investigation is hand-crafted, through standard operating procedures, fixed stages and role agents. Each is evaluated on its own data against few baselines, so it is unknown whether this design beats letting a capable model investigate on its own. We compare three simple harnesses that prescribe none of the model's calls (one call over an evidence package, a SQL agent and the Codex coding agent) with five published LLM RCA agents

items.title: WorldPager: Zero-Stall Tiered Memory for Long-Horizon World Models on a Single Consumer GPU
items.summary: Interactive world models keep the KV of past chunks as retrieval memory so that revisited places stay consistent. On a single consumer machine (one RTX 4090, 32 GiB of host memory, one NVMe SSD), long sessions with such memory hit two walls. The first is capacity: the KV of Matrix-Game 2.0 exhausts host memory after 45 seconds of video in bf16 and after 2.8 minutes in int4. The second is the model's positional horizon of 4.3 minutes. items.summary: Large organizations consume large language models (LLMs) from several vendors at once, each with its own API dialect, credential model, streaming protocol and pricing. Integrated directly, this heterogeneity yields credential sprawl, format lock-in, unbounded spend and inconsistent governance. items.title: Group-GEMM in XLA: Making Mixture-of-Experts Fast and Memory-Efficient
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have become a standard in most recent LLMs (DeepSeek, Grok-1, Llama-4, Gemini). items.title: Accelerating MONAI Digital-Pathology Pipelines on AMD Instinct™ GPUs with hipCIM
items.summary: A digital-pathology model is only as fast as the pipeline that feeds it. That’s simple to overlook when the conversation turns to network architectures and FLOPs, but on real whole-slide workloads the truth is stubborn: a great deal of the wall-clock time goes to reading gigapixel slides off disk and decoding them into the small tiles the model consumes. Speed up the model and leave the reader untouched, and the pipeline barely moves.
